section_summary: This section contains historical agreements granting Japanese firms manufacturing, sales, and patent rights for door controls, air brakes, ship hatch covers, engines, and the Renn iron-smelting process. The agreements specify territorial limits, technical assistance, payments, patent obligations, and dispute procedures. It ends with an amendment to the Renn agreement and a short record of payments.

subfiles.title: Supplemental power-operated door-control agreement between National Pneumatic and Mitsubishi Denki
subfiles.about: The supplemental agreement expands covered products and adjusts territorial and commission terms.
subfiles.summary: It extends the 1925 agreement to products later identified in writing, defines Mitsubishi’s territory, and permits a commission below ten percent when competition requires lower prices.

subfiles.title: National Pneumatic board resolution authorizing the supplemental agreement
subfiles.from: Duncan A. Talbot, National Pneumatic Company
subfiles.about: The board authorizes company officers to execute the Mitsubishi agreement.
subfiles.summary: Talbot certifies the August 13 board resolution authorizing Forman to sign and Talbot to attest the agreement.

subfiles.title: Westinghouse–Mitsubishi Denki air-brake agreement effective September 1934
subfiles.about: Westinghouse licenses brake manufacture and sales and provides technical information to Mitsubishi Denki.
subfiles.summary: The agreement grants rights in Japan, its dependencies, and Manchukuo, subject to a reservation for Kobe Seikosho and limits on exports, sublicensing, and use of Westinghouse’s name. It provides for technical data, plant visits, engineers, patent maintenance, and differentiated commissions on railway and other sales. It takes effect from September 5, 1934, with arbitration and governing-law provisions; the signatures bear later dates. The opening date is OCR-inconsistent with those dates.

subfiles.title: Westinghouse–Mitsubishi Denki air-brake agreement of 1924
subfiles.about: An earlier agreement licenses Mitsubishi Denki to manufacture and sell Westinghouse brake apparatus.
subfiles.summary: Westinghouse undertakes to supply manufacturing information and assistance, while Mitsubishi pays preparation costs and a ten percent commission on brake sales. The license covers Japan and its dependencies, reserves rights involving Kobe Seikosho, restricts sales and use of the Westinghouse name, and sets patent, accounting, arbitration, and termination terms. It is executed in Tokyo on September 5, 1924.

subfiles.title: Macgregor–Mitsubishi Zosen hatch-cover patent agreement
subfiles.from: Robert Macgregor and Macgregor & King Limited
subfiles.about: The vendors sell Japanese hatch-cover patent rights to Mitsubishi Zosen for a lump sum and continuing royalty.
subfiles.summary: Mitsubishi acquires Japanese Patent No. 86,963 and improvements for £2,500, with a sixpence-per-square-foot royalty on covers manufactured and fitted. The vendors promise drawings, technical information, and training.

subfiles.title: Saurer–Mitsubishi Jukogyo internal-combustion-engine license
subfiles.about: Saurer grants Mitsubishi rights to make and sell specified internal combustion engines in Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The license covers engines for road, rail, marine, and stationary use, with limited exceptions for light-motor sales and no aircraft use. Saurer must provide drawings, developments, training, and technical help; Mitsubishi owes 300,000 Swiss francs and a five percent royalty subject to a later annual minimum. The agreement sets territorial sales restrictions, patent-sharing rules, government-requested sublicensing, arbitration, and a term beginning July 1, 1937.

subfiles.title: Willy Salge–Mitsubishi Jukogyo Lentz marine-engine agreement
subfiles.from: Willy Salge & Co. Technische Gesellschaft m.b.H.
subfiles.about: The patentees license Mitsubishi to build Lentz-system marine steam engines.
subfiles.summary: Mitsubishi receives an exclusive Japanese building license for LES and LED engines and specified worldwide sales rights. The patentees supply drawings, training, and improvements in exchange for US$20,000, with no per-engine royalty. The agreement also addresses patent maintenance, operating reports, and courts in Tokyo or Berlin.

subfiles.title: Renn Process patent agreement cover page
subfiles.to: Mitsubishi Kogyo Kaisha, Ltd. and Kabushiki Kaisha Showa Seikosho
subfiles.about: The cover identifies the parties and subject of the following agreement.
subfiles.summary: Cover page for the Renn Process patent agreement.

subfiles.title: Friedrich Krupp Grusonwerk–Japanese smelters Renn Process patent agreement
subfiles.to: Mitsubishi Kogyo Kaisha, Ltd. and Showa Seikojo, Ltd.
subfiles.about: Grusonwerk transfers Renn Process patent rights and know-how for smelting operations in Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The agreement transfers specified patents and applications, shares technical knowledge, and permits commercial use of the rotary-kiln process in Japan, Manchukuo, and designated Mongolian areas. The smelters agree to pay £400,000, share part of sublicensing receipts, buy certain equipment, and arrange technical assistance and ore tests. Further articles cover improvements, secrecy, plant inspection, territorial limits, and German law. The text says the arrangement had been in force since September 14, 1937; this version bears a December 30 signature date.

subfiles.title: Appendix amending the Renn Process equipment-purchase terms
subfiles.from: Japanese-Manchurian Renn Process Patent Joint Association and Friedrich Krupp Grusonwerk A.G.
subfiles.about: The parties replace the original obligation to purchase all necessary kilns and accessories from Grusonwerk.
subfiles.summary: The association may make equipment in Japan or Manchukuo, pays RM 100,000 for the change, and retains Grusonwerk’s planning assistance.

subfiles.title: Record of Renn Process payments to Friedrich Krupp
subfiles.about: A short table records two payments concerning the process patent and Manchukuo rights.
subfiles.summary: Lists payments dated April 21, 1945 and August 22, 1944, totaling ¥312,955.55.
